clue.text: Heaney's was on the level — that of Hichens, in prison

definitions.meaning: Seamus Heaney's 1996 collection is titled The ... Level
Robert Hichens wrote the novel The ... in Prison

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are book titles with the answer missing: Heaney's The ___ Level and Hichens's The ___ in Prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes two titles: Heaney's poetry collection about the carpenter's bubble gauge and Hichens's 1908 novel.

clue.text: Underworld capo in the pipeline

definitions.meaning: the Roman god who rules the realm of the dead, its boss
the code name of the Second World War fuel pipeline laid under the English Channel (Pipe-Line Under The Ocean)

explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld capo' suggests a gangster, but it is the classical ruler of the dead; 'in the pipeline' is not 'coming soon' but the wartime fuel line's acronym name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of the dead heads Hades, and Operation PLUTO supplied petrol to Allied forces in Normandy through undersea pipes.

clue.text: Stage manager offers new surgeries

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of surgeries are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: A theatre's stage manager moonlights by opening some medical practices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SURGERIES into the French theatre word.
explanation.definitionFit: A régisseur is the person in charge of staging a theatre or ballet production, a French borrowing for a director or manager.

clue.text: Soft option for Gertrude's 13?

definitions.meaning: soft as in gentle, delicate or easily hurt
13 across is a page boy, also called 'buttons' in Britain; Gertrude Stein's book is ... Buttons, so this word is the one she chose to go with them

explanation.walkthrough: A 'buttons' is British slang for a page boy, which links 13-across to Gertrude Stein's Tender Buttons. 'Option' also hints that a tender is an offer put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender meat or feelings are soft and gentle, and Stein's title pairs the adjective with buttons, the British nickname for a page boy.

clue.text: Machos in disguise from Cooper

indicators.note: disguise changes how something looks, so the letters of machos in are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tough men from Cooper's novel are going about in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disguise' rearranges MACHOS IN. The definition leans on the title The Last of the Mohicans by James Fenimore Cooper.
explanation.definitionFit: James Fenimore Cooper wrote The Last of the Mohicans, so a tribe from Cooper's pages is the Native American people of that title.

clue.text: She wrote of love and the lover

definitions.text: She wrote of love and the lover

parts.words: She wrote of love and the lover
parts.note: points to a French woman novelist famous for a book titled The Lover (L'Amant) and for the screenplay Hiroshima mon amour

explanation.walkthrough: The Lover (L'Amant, 1984) won the Prix Goncourt; 'of love' nods to Hiroshima mon amour.
explanation.definitionFit: The French author of L'Amant (The Lover) and the screenplay Hiroshima mon amour wrote repeatedly about passion and desire.

clue.text: Maid Marian in Collins publication

parts.note: not Robin Hood's sweetheart but the unmarried heroine Marian in Wilkie Collins's novel The Woman in White

explanation.walkthrough: 'Maid Marian' wants Robin Hood, and 'Collins' could be the publisher; instead it is Wilkie Collins and his spinster heroine, the surname being needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Marian Halcombe is the unmarried half-sister of Laura Fairlie in The Woman in White, Wilkie Collins's 1859 sensation novel.

clue.text: Chef begins with cooked rice makes pig out of some sailors

definitions.text: makes pig out of some sailors

indicators.note: begins means only the opening letter of the word Chef is used
cooked suggests the letters of rice are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A chef starts with cooked rice and turns some sailors into pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'begins' takes C from Chef; 'cooked' rearranges RICE into IRCE.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Odyssey the enchantress on Aeaea transforms Odysseus's crewmen into swine, which is exactly turning sailors into pigs.

clue.text: Ghastly innate pun relating to Poseidon

indicators.note: ghastly suggests something mangled, so the letters of innate pun are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful built-in pun about the Greek sea god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ghastly' rearranges INNATE PUN. Poseidon's Roman equivalent is Neptune.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is the Roman counterpart of the Greek sea god Poseidon, so the adjective formed from Neptune means connected with him.

clue.text: "However confident he may be that he has — led a woman, a man likes to have reassurance …" (Bachelors Anonymous, P.G. Wodehouse)

definitions.text: "However confident he may be that he has — led a woman, a man likes to have reassurance …" (Bachelors Anonymous, P.G. Wodehouse)

parts.words: "However confident he may be that he has — led a woman, a man likes to have reassurance …" (Bachelors Anonymous, P.G. Wodehouse)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-gap quotation: the missing verb, with the printed -led, means outwitted or outmanoeuvred in tactics

explanation.walkthrough: The dash stands for the missing word; with '-led' attached it forms the past tense of a military verb for beating someone through better strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: To outgeneral someone is to beat them by superior tactics, as a better commander would, which fits winning over a woman in Wodehouse's quip.

clue.text: Pope's method of undoing a lock

definitions.text: Pope's method of undoing a lock

parts.words: Pope's method of undoing a lock
parts.note: not a pontiff picking a lock but Alexander Pope's mock-epic poem about the theft of a curl of hair

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope' looks papal and 'lock' looks like a door fastening; it is Alexander Pope's 1712 poem in which Lord Petre snips a lock of Arabella Fermor's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: In The R___ of the Lock, the old sense of the word is seizure or carrying off, here of a lock of hair.

clue.text: Judge of Jean-Jacques

parts.note: points to the Genevan philosopher's late dialogues, titled with his own surname followed by Judge of Jean-Jacques, in which he defends himself

explanation.walkthrough: The philosopher wrote a set of dialogues titled '___, Judge of Jean-Jacques', setting himself as judge over his own first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genevan thinker Jean-Jacques wrote dialogues (1772-76) in which his surname-self sits in judgement on his first-name self.

clue.text: Yes, it is a dagger that you see before you

definitions.text: Yes, it is a dagger that you see before you

parts.words: Yes, it is a dagger that you see before you
parts.note: echoes Macbeth's 'Is this a dagger which I see before me?' but the dagger is the printer's mark, which has this name

explanation.walkthrough: The Macbeth echo leads to a weapon, but the dagger meant is the typographical mark (†) set on the page in front of the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: The printer's dagger sign, used for footnotes, is also called an obelisk, and the older Greek-derived name is the one wanted here.

clue.text: Rich Windsor gentleman turned by readers

definitions.meaning: Master George ..., a wealthy citizen in Shakespeare's The Merry Wives of Windsor
a leaf of a book, which readers flip over as they go

explanation.walkthrough: 'Windsor gentleman' may suggest royalty; it is a character in The Merry Wives of Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Merry Wives has a well-off townsman named Master Page, and a book's leaves are what readers flip.

clue.text: Singing by two choirs apparently opposed to fake

parts.note: someone opposed to a thing is anti it
phony means fake or sham, the American spelling

explanation.surface: Two choirs singing seem set against something false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' flags that the split into 'against' plus 'sham' is a joke, not the true etymology.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiphony is responsive singing in which two choirs or halves of a choir alternate verses.

clue.text: Comic writer may betray bias with Lear

indicators.note: betraying something gives away its true form, so the letters of bias and Lear are rearranged

explanation.surface: A comic author reveals his prejudice by taking on King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may betray' rearranges BIAS and LEAR, with 'with' joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: François Rabelais, author of Gargantua and Pantagruel, is the great French comic satirist of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Tragic ballad figure in history play walk-on

definitions.meaning: the hero of an old English ballad who returns to find his love has died of grief, then dies himself
Lovel is a minor lord in Shakespeare's Richard III with only a few lines

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links the two definitions. Both are the same title and surname: the ballad's lord and Shakespeare's minor noble in Richard III.
explanation.definitionFit: The Child Ballad tells of a nobleman whose sweetheart dies while he is away, and Shakespeare's Richard III gives a nobleman of that name a small part.

clue.text: Whose plays likely to figure in this lexicon?

definitions.text: Whose plays likely to figure in this lexicon?

parts.words: Whose plays likely to figure in this lexicon?
parts.note: the Jacobean dramatist John who wrote The Duchess of Malfi shares his surname with the American dictionary maker Noah

explanation.walkthrough: 'Whose plays' are John Webster's; the lexicon is Noah Webster's dictionary, so the plays belong in it by name.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive covers both the dramatist John Webster's plays and Noah Webster's American dictionary.

clue.text: Most firm in Shandy man's way

parts.note: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy, so the Shandy man is Sterne, here possessive
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Tristram Shandy's author was at his most resolute on his own road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. 'Shandy' looks like the beer and lemonade drink; it is Tristram Shandy.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of stern means strictest or most severe and unyielding.

clue.text: Associated with book by Browning

parts.note: Robert Browning's long poem pairs this word with 'the Book' in its title

explanation.walkthrough: Browning's verse novel is The ___ and the Book (1868-69), about a murder trial in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Browning's title joins this word to 'the Book'; it also means a circle of associates, which 'Associated' hints at.

clue.text: More dramas

parts.note: not a request for extra plays but the plays of Hannah More, whose collection was titled with this word before Dramas

explanation.walkthrough: 'More' looks like 'extra'; it is Hannah More, whose 1782 collection was Sacred Dramas.
explanation.definitionFit: Hannah More published Sacred Dramas, plays on Bible stories for the young, so her dramas are holy ones.

clue.text: Works like Romeo and Juliet, Othello and Hamlet, for example

definitions.text: Works like Romeo and Juliet, Othello and Hamlet, for example

parts.words: Works like Romeo and Juliet, Othello and Hamlet, for example
parts.note: these are Shakespeare plays, but each was also set to music by Gounod, Verdi and Thomas

explanation.walkthrough: The titles point to plays, but the works meant are the sung versions by Gounod, Verdi and Ambroise Thomas.
explanation.definitionFit: Gounod's Roméo et Juliette, Verdi's Otello and Thomas's Hamlet are all staged musical dramas, each with an orchestra and sung throughout.

clue.text: Anger created by ungrateful child

indicators.note: created suggests making something new from the letters of anger

explanation.walkthrough: 'created' rearranges ANGER; 'by' links it to the definition, Lear's second daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: In King Lear the old king's second daughter turns on him after he gives her half his kingdom, the very picture of a thankless offspring.

clue.text: Lifeless part of verse just reached by tardy poet?

parts.note: lifeless means dead
a line is one row of a poem

explanation.surface: A late poet only just meets the cutoff with a dull bit of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a late writer only just makes the cutoff, and the parts are poetic too.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutoff time for submitting work is what a late writer barely manages to meet.

clue.text: Star identified by Binyon and Innes

definitions.text: Star identified by Binyon and Innes

parts.words: Star identified by Binyon and Innes
parts.note: the pole star's name is the title of works by Laurence Binyon and by Hammond Innes

explanation.walkthrough: Hammond Innes's novel North Star (1974) and Laurence Binyon's poem share the pole star's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the pole star, is commonly called by the compass point it marks, which both writers used as a title.

clue.text: Youthful in Holland, was she afraid to run away?

definitions.text: was she afraid to run away?
definitions.meaning: the American novelist Erica who wrote Fear of Flying, flying read as fleeing

explanation.walkthrough: 'afraid to run away' twists 'fear of flying' into fear of fleeing, pointing to Erica Jong's 1973 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch adjective means young, and the author of Fear of Flying shares the surname.

clue.text: Richard Woodville real upset by flowers

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of real are tipped into a new order

parts.note: in crosswords a flower is something that flows, a river

explanation.surface: A man named Richard is truly distressed by a bunch of blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges REAL into EARL; 'flowers' is the crossword joke for rivers, things that flow. 'by' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Woodville, father of Edward IV's queen Elizabeth, was created the first holder of that title in 1466.

clue.text: Sleepy god is seen in clinical procedure

parts.note: Hypnos is the Greek god of sleep

explanation.surface: The Greek god of slumber turns up in a medical operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Induced trance is used therapeutically by doctors and psychologists, so it counts as a medical technique.

clue.text: Riddler's retreat

parts.note: the home of the oracle of Apollo, whose priestess gave famously cryptic answers

explanation.walkthrough: The 'Riddler' is not the Batman villain but the Pythia, Apollo's oracle, who spoke in riddles from her shrine on Mount Parnassus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek sanctuary on Parnassus housed Apollo's oracle, whose ambiguous pronouncements were riddles.
